name: Shezan

global_influences.evidence: Secondary press (bdhiphop.com) describes his style as combining hip-hop production and rap delivery conventions with traditional Bengali sounds — East/West fusion rather than a single named influence.

local_adaptation_notes: Music press describes Shezan's style as blending hip-hop with traditional Bengali sonic elements, positioned as part of the broader Bangla rap wave rather than an imitation of a Western regional style.
sound_evolution_summary: Rose to wider recognition via the collaboration "Marattok Madarchod" with 1230 Klassick, followed by singles including "Cartel", "Player", "Jonggol", "Seal Maar", "Blacklist", "Outlawz", "Duno Mono Tino", and "DISS-COUNT", building toward the debut album Laal Batti, which features collaborations with Nizam Rabby, Gunshot Player, and fellow-catalogued artist Hannan (`hannan`).
concert_culture_notes: Not yet documented in available sources.
listener_community_notes: Active within two hip-hop production/artist collectives, Killaz Kulture and Wrong Side; as a producer under Killaz Kulture he has produced beats for other Bangladeshi hip-hop artists (Shafayat Hossain, Sheikh Sadi, Akib Bro, Muhammad Abdullah), placing him as a connective node between multiple artists in the contemporary hip-hop scene — relevant for future BMPN edges once collaboration/production-credit data is incorporated.
